generic_webhook.name: Webhook Trigger

subBlocks.title: Setup Instructions
subBlocks.defaultValue:
1. Copy the webhook URL and use it in your external service or API.
2. Configure your service to send webhooks to this URL.
3. The webhook accepts POST. Turn on "Accept Other HTTP Methods" to also accept GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE — for example to trigger the workflow from a link in an email.
4. Body fields are available in your workflow, and URL query parameters under "query" (for example "query.id"). Turn on "Expose Request Headers" to also get "headers" (for example "headers.x-event-name"), and "Accept Other HTTP Methods" to also get "method".
5. Authentication is header-based, so it cannot be used with a plain link. If authentication is enabled, include the token in the Secret Header Name you configured, or in "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" if you left it blank — only the configured one is accepted, not either.
6. To deduplicate incoming events, set the Deduplication Field to the dot-notation path of a unique identifier in the payload (e.g. "event.id"). Duplicate values within 7 days will be skipped.
7. Enable "Verify Test Events" only if the sending service needs a temporary 200 response while validating the webhook URL.

event_type.description: Type of Slack payload: an Events API event (e.g., app_mention, message), an interactivity type (e.g., block_actions), or "slash_command" for slash commands

subtype.description: Message subtype (e.g., channel_join, channel_leave, bot_message, file_share). Null for regular user messages

channel.description: Slack channel ID where the event occurred

channel_type.description: Type of channel (e.g., channel, group, im, mpim). Useful for distinguishing DMs from public channels

user.description: User ID who triggered the event

bot_id.description: Bot ID if the message was sent by a bot. Null for human users

text.description: Message text content. For slash commands, the text after the command. For interactivity, the source message text (falls back to the triggering action value)

timestamp.description: Message timestamp from the triggering event

thread_ts.description: Parent thread timestamp (if message is in a thread)

streaming_message_ts.description: Message timestamps streamed during a stopped agent session

tab.description: App Home tab that was opened, including messages for Agent View

context.description: Current Agent View context. Normalized from context on app_context_changed/app_home_opened or app_context on message.im

user_team_id.description: Slack workspace/team ID of the user who triggered the event. Used for Slack Connect response streaming.

reaction.description: Emoji reaction name (e.g., thumbsup). Present for reaction_added/reaction_removed events

item_user.description: User ID of the original message author. Present for reaction_added/reaction_removed events

command.description: Slash command name including the leading slash (e.g., /deploy). Present for slash commands

action_id.description: action_id of the first interactive element triggered. Present for block_actions (button/select clicks)

action_value.description: Value carried by the first interactive element (button value, selected option, date, etc.). Present for block_actions

actions.description: Full array of interactive actions from the payload, preserving every element and its value. Present for block_actions

response_url.description: Temporary URL to post a response back to the originating message or command. Present for interactivity and slash commands

trigger_id.description: Short-lived trigger ID used to open a modal in response. Present for interactivity and slash commands

callback_id.description: Callback ID of the shortcut or view. Present for shortcuts and modal submissions

api_app_id.description: Slack app ID. Present for interactivity and slash commands

app_id.description: App ID of the app that produced the event (e.g. the bot that posted a message). Used to identify the app's own output

message_ts.description: Timestamp of the message the interaction originated from. Present for block_actions

view.description: Full Slack view object for modal interactions: state.values (submitted input values), private_metadata, id, callback_id, and hash. Present for view_submission/view_closed; null otherwise

message.description: Full source message object the interaction came from, including its blocks and text. Present for block_actions on a message; null otherwise

state.description: Current values of all stateful elements in the surface (state.values) at the time of a block action — e.g. inputs read on a button click. Present for block_actions; null otherwise

hasFiles.description: Whether the message has file attachments

files.description: File attachments downloaded from the message (if includeFiles is enabled and bot token is provided)
